newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSTANT VIEW - RBNZ economic projections.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - RBNZ economic projections.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's economic projections on Thursday in which the bank said monetary conditions had become inappropriately firm.
ADRIAN ORR, CHIEF ECONOMIST, NATIONAL BANK OF NZ LTD
"They're saying conditions had tightened in advance of what they desired in December. All they wanted was no change in conditions, yet they had tightened.

"They have gone a little bit further than that as well, in the sense that they're now forecasting on average inflation in 1998 around the 0.8, 0.9 percent level, which is still well below their 1.5 (the mid-point of the bank's 0-3 percent inflation target range).
"They are saying yes, there is some cautious scope for further easing even from here, but only once we see the whites of the eyes of lower inflation."
Bills had only come off around 25 basis points but if the bank's 2:1 trade-off ratio between bank bills and the TWI was in action then bills should have come off around 75 basis points, he said.
"It indicates a little bit of scepticism about the numbers which make up the trade-off."
Garlick does not expect bank bills yields to fall much further.
"The statement was not really a surprise except the comments about easing which amount to quite a bit of fine tuning.
"That is perhaps a touch unrealistic given the day-to-day fluctuation of the market.
"The economic forecasts themselves look reasonably plausible. I don't think they are too questionable.
"The main thing is that they have called for an easing on this monetary conditions index that they have published.
"It's a pretty mechanical view of the world and they are perhaps placing an unrealistic amount of weight on that."
